objective: Proof. (i) Signed Seymour lemma: a minimal not-all-equal-unsatisfiable signed system has at least as many lines as points, and with equality its signed incidence pattern is sign-nonsingular. (ii) In a k-regular k-uniform system a minimal failing subsystem is a union of components with as many lines as points. (iii) Its incidence pattern is not sign-nonsingular, because the digraph of a k-regular bipartite graph has in- and out-degree k - 1 >= 3 and is even (Thomassen 1992). So signed not-all-equal never fails on k-regular k-uniform systems for k >= 4; at k = 3 it fails exactly on the knot's Pfaffian spaces. Check exhaustively for k = 4, n <= 7, with every signing.
status: Proved by FOUR-PLACE-20261031-001B-P001: for every k >= 4 signed not-all-equal never fails on k-regular k-uniform systems: a minimal failing signed system is square with a sign-nonsingular pattern (signed Seymour lemma), regularity makes it a union of components, and its digraph (in- and out-degree k - 1 >= 3) is even by Thomassen (1992), so the pattern is not sign-nonsingular; at k = 3 the failures are exactly the knot's Pfaffian spaces; checked k = 4 (n <= 7, every signing), k = 5 (n = 5, 6), no sign-nonsingular 4-regular pattern for n <= 7, rigidity of pieces to five internal points
title: Value-free not-all-equal never fails on k-regular systems for k >= 4
